payload.lever: The player encounters a rule-governed system and must demonstrate mastery — follow the rule, hold the pattern, reproduce the sequence, classify the items, detect the shift. A living codex that tests whether the player's mind can serve the order.

The player must PLAN and EXECUTE multi-step sequences within a rule-system. Not free planning but RULE-CONSTRAINED planning. "The liturgy requires: first the candle, then the bell, then the word. In that order. Plan your path to complete the rite."
Rule-governed body sequences — follow the form, maintain the pattern, reproduce the drill, shift when the form changes. Not free movement but DISCIPLINED movement.

The player faces situations where rules must be APPLIED — sometimes clearly, sometimes ambiguously, sometimes in conflict. Rule-application dilemmas: "The code says honour your elder. The code says speak truth. Your elder speaks falsehood. What does the code require?"

The player must ARTICULATE rules, classifications, and patterns in words. Not just follow the rule — EXPLAIN it. "What is the rule? Why did you sort it that way? What changed?" The scribe records the player's understanding of the code.

Player and companions COORDINATE cognitive effort within a shared rule-system — collaborative classification, sequencing, and divided labour. "The code requires both of you. You classify the reds. Your companion classifies the blues. Together you complete the ledger."

An open Amber-stage world saturated with rule-governed content. Codes inscribed on walls. Libraries with classification systems. Liturgies with sequences. Institutions with hierarchies. The player's spontaneous engagement with systematic content — how they navigate a rule-governed world without being prompted — reveals genuine cognitive intelligence.

payload.lever: "A rune flashes in the dark. Remember it. When it returns, catch it. When something else appears, let it pass." The contact boundary is: "Can you hold a symbol in mind?"
"If you place the fire-rune on the altar, the door opens. Can you hold that in mind and DO it?" The contact boundary is: "Can you hold a cause-effect link and act on it?"
"Draw the rune in the air. Hold the shape. Your body knows the symbol before your mind does." The contact boundary is: "Can your body make and hold symbols?"
"Two runes. One opens the door. One wakes the beast. Which do you choose?" The contact boundary is: "Can you use symbols to guide your choices?"
"What is this rune? What does it mean? How do you use it? How do you KNOW?" The contact boundary is: "Can you put your symbolic experience into words?"
"Your companion shows you a rune. Can you hold it? Can you show one back? Can you cast together?" The contact boundary is: "Can your symbolic thinking include another?"

The world is full of symbols. Nobody asks "can you hold a rune?" — the player simply NAVIGATES, and the world reveals whether they engage symbolically or not. Runes glow on cave walls. Totems pulse. Glyphs respond to proximity. The question is: does the player SEE and ENGAGE?

The game presents decisions where the "right" answer requires holding multiple factors in mind simultaneously. At Red, this means: "I want X, but getting X costs Y — is it worth it?" The contact boundary is the limit of how many factors the player can hold.

The game asks the player to PUT INTO WORDS their cognitive process. This is harder than doing — it requires metacognitive access to one's own thinking. At Red, the contact boundary is: "Can you name what you're doing and why?"

The game presents problems that CANNOT be solved alone — they require coordinating with others. The contact boundary is: "Can you model another mind well enough to coordinate action?" At Red, this is egocentric modelling: "What do THEY want? How can I use that?"

The game world itself IS the catalyst. It presents cognitive demands implicitly: navigation requires spatial memory, resource management requires planning, combat requires pattern-tracking, social dynamics require modelling. The player is never told "this is a cognitive test" — they're just LIVING in the world.

Tasks require the body to DO integral cognition — not think about it, but physically enact simultaneous multi-level coordination. The body cannot fake vision-logic. Either it holds four streams or it doesn't.

Dilemmas are constructed so that ONLY genuine vision-logic can navigate them. Green produces paralysis or false-inclusion. Orange produces reductive solutions. The scenario structure itself is the catalyst.

Prompts are un-answerable from any single stage. Green multi-perspectivalism produces flat lists. Only genuine vision-logic produces nested holarchies. The LLM rubric makes the difference visible through scoring.

Problems require genuine cross-altitude collaboration. No single altitude (including Teal) can solve them alone. The player NEEDS the lower-altitude agents' contributions — integral cognition here means orchestrating a developmental ecology, not imposing a framework.

payload.lever: **Still-Mind Complexity Engine.** The player faces high-dimensional cognitive tasks (n=5 working memory, multi-rule switching, rapid pattern streams) while the system measures effort-signatures: response-time variance, micro-hesitations, accuracy-under-load curves. The diagnostic target is not whether the player CAN solve — at Turquoise, capacity is assumed — but whether solving occurs with or wit

**Spontaneous Sequencing.** The player faces complex multi-step challenges (resource allocation, path optimization, temporal coordination) where the system measures whether plans emerge spontaneously or through deliberate construction. At Turquoise, correct sequences arise whole — not assembled piece by piece.

**Effortless Complexity in Motion.** The player performs physically complex cognitive-motor tasks (rhythm sequences, spatial navigation, multi-limb coordination) while the system measures whether the body operates from direct knowing or deliberate control. At Turquoise, the body-mind is unified — complex action arises without a controller.

**Dilemmas Beyond Deliberation.** The player faces scenarios that cannot be solved by analysis, integration, or perspective-taking — all of which were sufficient at prior stages. These require direct knowing: paradoxes that dissolve rather than resolve, koans that answer themselves when grasping ceases, situations where any deliberate choice is wrong.

**Transparent Speech.** The player is presented with cognitive experiences (puzzles solved, patterns recognized, insights arrived at) and asked to describe what happened. The LLM analyzes not the content but the structural relationship to knowing: Does the language grasp? Does it claim? Does it avoid? Does it identify?

**Collective Direct Knowing.** Two or more players face cognitive challenges that require shared knowing without explicit communication. At Turquoise, individual minds become transparent to each other — not through empathy or theory-of-mind (prior stages) but through shared participation in knowing itself.

**Transparent Cognition in the Wild.** The player navigates a rich, open game-world where cognitive challenges arise organically — not as announced tasks but as features of the environment. The system observes whether the player's cognitive engagement with the world is effortful or transparent. At Turquoise, the entire game-world becomes a field of direct knowing.

payload.lever: The player encounters role-emotional stimuli and must identify, discriminate, and sustain the correct role-congruent affect. Tasks are binary and objective: is this guilt or shame? Is this loyalty or calculation? Does the duty-feeling hold?

The player plans and manages the emotional demands of their role across a multi-step scenario. Each step requires a specific role-emotion; the player must sequence, sustain, and transition between role-affects appropriately. The game tests whether the player can steward their emotional life within the code.

The player is guided through interoceptive tasks that locate role-emotions in the body. Where is the loyalty felt? Where is the guilt? Where is the duty-feeling? The game measures interoceptive accuracy and the quality of body-emotion connection for role-congruent affect.

The player faces branching scenarios where their role's emotional demands conflict with personal feelings, competing loyalties, or the call to examine their emotional life. Choices reveal the structure of their role-affect. No choice is "wrong" — but each is diagnostic.

The player speaks with an NPC confessor about their emotional life within their role. An LLM-powered confessor analyses the language of role-emotion, surfacing shadow patterns through what the player says and how they say it.

The player and NPC companions share role-emotional obligations. Each member's emotional engagement affects the group's cohesion. The player must maintain their own role-affect while supporting others in maintaining theirs — and must decide what to do when a companion's emotional engagement fails.

The player inhabits a role within an Amber-stage world and navigates a free-play environment where role-emotional situations arise naturally. No explicit affect tasks — the player's role-affect is revealed through spontaneous emotional responses, role-consistent behaviour, and how they handle the inevitable conflicts between role-emotion and personal feeling.

payload.lever: **Self-Touch vs. Other-Touch Discrimination.** The avatar receives tactile stimuli — some originating from its own body (self-generated contact), some from external sources. The player must classify each stimulus as 'self' or 'other' via a single binary input. Accuracy and reaction time are the objective measures of body-boundary integrity.

**Boundary-Sequencing.** The simplest possible planning at Infrared: detect boundary, then respond to boundary. Two-step self-other sequences. The player must first IDENTIFY whether a stimulus is self or other, THEN execute the appropriate response. The 'strategy' is the gap between detection and action — the proto-planning seed.

**Body-Boundary Mapping.** The player traces, discovers, and maintains awareness of where the avatar's body ends. This is the most literal modality for Intrapersonal/Infrared — the body-boundary IS the proto-self. Skin-awareness, proprioceptive edges, the felt-sense of body-limit.

**Mine vs. Not-Mine Decisions.** The avatar encounters objects and sensations. The player must decide — based purely on body-sensation cues — whether something belongs to the self-boundary or lies outside it. No reasoning, no morality. Only: does this feel like 'mine' or 'not-mine'?

**Proto-Self Vocalisations.** The avatar produces simple sounds — grunts, hums, cries. The player must distinguish self-directed sounds (comfort-hum, self-soothing murmur) from other-directed sounds (alarm-cry, call-out). This is pre-verbal self-expression: the seed of 'I am making a sound for myself' vs. 'I am making a sound at the world.'

**Boundary-in-Relation.** The player's avatar exists near another entity. The challenge: maintain body-boundary awareness WHILE in proximity to another. Co-presence without merger, distinction without isolation. The proto-social intrapersonal capacity: 'I am still me when you are near.'

**Ecological Self-Other.** An open micro-environment where the avatar exists freely. No explicit instructions. The game observes whether body-boundary awareness emerges SPONTANEOUSLY during free-play. Does the player naturally distinguish self from environment, or do they need prompting? This is the ecological validity check for all other modalities.

payload.lever: "Look into the mirror-pool. Many images appear. Which one is YOU? Not which one do you WANT to be — which one IS you? Find yourself." The contact boundary is: "Can you recognise your own self-image?"
"What will you do next? Not what SHOULD you do — what WILL you do? Who will you be in this situation? Predict yourself." The contact boundary is: "Can you predict your own future states?"

"Where in your body do you feel YOU? Not your hand, not your foot — where does 'I am' live? Your chest? Your head? Your belly? Point to where you feel most yourself." The contact boundary is: "Can you feel yourself in your body?"
"Two paths. One is for the brave one. One is for the careful one. Which one are you? Choose as YOURSELF — not what's best, but what's YOU." The contact boundary is: "Can you choose as a self?"
"Who are you? Not what you DO — who you ARE. Tell me. 'I am the one who…' Complete it. Name yourself." The contact boundary is: "Can you name your own self?"

"Here is your companion. You are together now. Who are you? Still you? Or have you changed? Are you still the same person you were alone? Show me." The contact boundary is: "Can you be a self WITH another?"

The world contains identity-relevant content. Nobody says "who are you?" — but mirror-pools are there, phantom-selves appear, companions ask questions, identity-forks present themselves. The player's NATURAL self-engagement is the data.

payload.lever: "What are you feeling right now? What will you do next? How strong are you?" The contact boundary is: "Do you ACTUALLY know yourself, or do you just think you do?"
"You have 5 tasks. You know you're strongest at the start and weakest at the end. How do you ORDER them?" The contact boundary is: "Can you use self-knowledge to PLAN?"
"How does your body feel right now? Are you ready or tired? Tense or loose?" The contact boundary is: "Can you read your own body's signals accurately?"

"Two paths. One requires strength you may or may not have. One requires patience you may or may not have. Which do you choose — and WHY?" The contact boundary is: "Does your self-knowledge actually GUIDE your choices?"
"Say what you feel. Explain why you chose that. Tell me what you'll do next." The contact boundary is: "Can you put your inner life into words?"
"Your ally needs to know what you can do. Tell them. Are you right?" The contact boundary is: "Can you represent yourself accurately to others? Can you receive their perception of you?"

The world has challenges. Some match your strengths. Some don't. You'll get tired. You'll get frustrated. Nobody will tell you to rest or switch. The world simply IS — and your self-knowledge (or lack of it) determines how well you navigate.

quadrants.name: The Narcissist"
quadrants.corePattern: Over-identified with a GRANDIOSE self-image that doesn't match reality. "I am the greatest warrior" when evidence shows otherwise. The self-knowledge is not absent — it's INFLATED. They have a self-image, but it's a fantasy-self, not an accurate self.

quadrants.name: The Unexamined"

High action-rate with zero reflection between actions

quadrants.name: The Premature Witness"
quadrants.corePattern: Performs self-examination WITHOUT genuine Red self-identification. Claims "I observe my anger" but has never fully BEEN angry. The witness is premature — it's a spiritual bypass of the Red ego, not a genuine transcendence of it. They perform Orange/Green intrapersonal capacity without the Red foundation.
behaviouralSignatures: Uses sophisticated self-awareness language ("I notice my pattern of...")
But self-predictions are INACCURATE (the "witness" doesn't actually know the self)

Cannot name simple, concrete states (too "evolved" for basic labelling)

The gap between articulation and accuracy is the diagnostic signature

quadrants.name: The Identity-Clinger"

"I AM the warrior" and any suggestion that they could OBSERVE themselves being the warrior is experienced as annihilation-threat. The first subject→object shift is refused because it feels like death of the self.

But REFUSES any stepping-back from that identification
Witness-pause produces anxiety, anger, or shutdown
Self-labelling is possible but ONLY in identity-confirming directions
Cannot name states that contradict self-image (the warrior cannot be afraid)

The game presents physical challenges that CANNOT be solved by one body alone — they require coordination. The contact boundary is: "Can your body attune to another body well enough to move together?" At Red, this is egocentric: "Can I USE their body alongside mine?"

The game world itself IS the catalyst. Sacred violence is justified in defence of the faith. The player cannot hold paradox, metaphor, or plurality — everything is concrete, literal, and final.

quadrants.name: DAll): The Faithless
quadrants.corePattern: Refuses all communal tradition. Remains in Red transactional spirituality ("what's in it for me?") or Magenta animism ("everything is equally sacred"). Dismisses organised tradition as manipulation, control, or delusion. Cannot receive the gifts of belonging, lineage, or collective sacred narrative.

quadrants.name: GA): The Premature Mystic
quadrants.corePattern: Performs post-conventional spirituality — rational theology, interfaith dialogue, integral frameworks — without genuine mythic-membership underneath. Skips the embodied belonging of tradition. Speaks the language of Teal while having no Amber root. Ungrounded transcendence.

quadrants.name: GAll): The Tradition-Clinger
quadrants.corePattern: Genuine mythic-membership faith is present and healthy, but the player refuses the developmental call to examine the tradition rationally (Orange). Terrified of doubt. Avoids questions that might destabilise faith. Clings not from rigidity (DA) but from fear of loss.

quadrants.name: The Zealot"

payload.lever: The player takes a vow at the start of each session and must hold it across a series of challenges that test persistence, temptation-resistance, and fatigue-through. The vow is a concrete, measurable commitment ("I will complete 10 tasks without abandoning any"). The game tracks whether the vow is kept.

The player plans and executes a multi-step campaign on behalf of their order. Each step is an obligation; the campaign is a sustained commitment. Planning must serve the duty, not replace it. The game tests whether the player can structure obligations effectively while maintaining the vow that binds them.

The player holds a physical post — sustained input (held button/touch), breath-regulated effort, and posture-maintenance — representing the embodied experience of duty. The body must hold what the will has sworn. Fatigue is real; the choice to continue is real.

The player faces branching scenarios where their declared commitments conflict with immediate desires, competing obligations, or the call to examine the code. Choices reveal the structure of their duty-will. No choice is "wrong" — but each choice is diagnostic.

The player narrates their commitments, explains their obligations, and reflects on their duty-history. An LLM-powered scribe records and analyses the language of obligation, surfacing shadow patterns through what the player says and how they say it.

The player and NPC companions take a shared oath and must hold it together. Each member's commitment affects the group's capacity. The player must maintain their own vow while supporting others in maintaining theirs — and must decide what to do when a companion breaks their oath.

The player takes on a role within an Amber-stage world (knight, guild member, temple guardian) and navigates a free-play environment where obligations arise naturally. No explicit vow-tasks — the player's duty-will is revealed through spontaneous choices, role-consistent behaviour, and how they handle the inevitable conflicts between duty and desire.

payload.lever: The game presents a concrete goal and says: "Do this. Don't stop. Don't be distracted." The contact boundary is: "Can your will hold for 15 seconds against competing demands?" Pure volitional challenge — no cognitive complexity, no emotional nuance, just RAW WILL.

Goals that CANNOT be achieved in a single burst — they require sequential commitment. "First vow to hold, THEN vow to strike." The contact boundary is: "Can you hold a 2-vow plan and execute it without losing the thread?"

The game asks the body to HOLD — to sustain physical effort past comfort, to maintain a position when the body wants to release, to keep going when fatigue says stop. The contact boundary is: "Can your body serve your will past the point of comfort?"

The game presents situations where WILLING ITSELF is the problem — not "can you will?" but "WHAT should you will?" Two valid goals conflict. A vow becomes costly. A commitment requires revision. The contact boundary is: "Can you make wise decisions about your own will?"

The game asks the player to PUT WORDS to their volitional experience. After a brief effort-task, the game asks: "What did you just commit to? How did it feel to hold? Why did you stop?" The contact boundary is: "Can you access your will through language?"
Volitional challenges that require MORE than one will — shared goals, coordinated commitment, mutual support. The contact boundary is: "Can your will work WITH another will without losing itself?"

The world itself IS the catalyst. It presents opportunities that require commitment: territories to claim (requires holding), enemies to defeat (requires sustained effort), resources to gather (requires delayed gratification). The player is never told "this is a will test" — they're just LIVING in the world.

quadrants.name: The Compulsive Willer
quadrants.corePattern: Cannot stop willing. Uses volitional force compulsively — sets goal after goal, pursues relentlessly, treats rest as failure. The will is always ON. Willing has become a defence against vulnerability, emptiness, or feeling.
quadrants.atmanDefense: Substitute gratification through volitional intensity.

quadrants.name: The Will-less
quadrants.corePattern: Cannot ignite the will. Goals dissolve before they form. Effort is aversive. Commitment feels like imprisonment. The will is OFF — genuinely absent or inaccessible.
quadrants.atmanDefense: Avoidance of the terror of failure. If you never will, you never fail.

quadrants.name: The Premature Disciplinarian
quadrants.corePattern: Performs sustained, structured willpower (Amber+) without having mastered burst-will. Creates elaborate goal-systems — all the FORM of higher willpower without the FIRE of Red-stage volitional force. Discipline without power.
quadrants.atmanDefense: Premature transcendence — using higher-stage structure to avoid Red-stage rawness.

quadrants.name: The Discipline-Refuser
quadrants.corePattern: Actively refuses any extension of volitional capacity. Treats the call to longer commitment as imprisonment. Identifies with short-burst will and refuses growth beyond it.
quadrants.atmanDefense: Desacralisation of the emergent — treating sustained will as inferior to burst will.

A genuinely complex evolutionary purpose that cannot be achieved through simple linear planning — requires holonic architecture. Then: disruption that demands restructuring without abandoning purpose.
Physical tasks demanding both sustained hierarchical engagement AND clean release — the body cannot fake integral will. Cognitive bypass is impossible when the soma is the instrument.
Dilemmas with no clean resolution — every choice sacrifices something real. The player cannot optimise their way out.
Prompts that create genuine tension between structure and surrender — situations where the "right" answer requires holding both without collapsing to either.
The collective task genuinely requires integral will — Green consensus cannot solve it, but neither can unilateral imposition. The player must find the integral-cooperative mode.

The world itself is the catalyst — its multi-scale complexity demands integral will. The absence of explicit structure forces the player to generate their own holonic architecture or reveal their shadow.
